quizName: DMV Practice Test #13 25 Questions • Passing Score 18

questions.question: When riding at night, which of the following should you NOT do?

options.text: Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to help you see.
Ride only in the left portion of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride only in the left portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: When riding at night, use your high beam (unless you are following or meeting another car), use the headlights of other vehicles to help you see, and wear reflective materials to stay visible. Change your lane position as needed to see, be seen, and keep a safe distance from other vehicles.

questions.question: On a slippery surface, which of the following should you NOT do?

options.text: Use only the front brake when slowing or stopping.
Use both brakes when slowing or stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use only the front brake when slowing or stopping.
questions.explanation: To ride safely on a slippery surface, use both brakes when slowing or stopping, slow down, and avoid sudden moves. Watch out for oily areas, dirt, gravel, shaded areas, and bridges, as these surfaces are more slippery than others.

questions.question: When stopping behind a vehicle, you should:

options.text: Stop far behind the vehicle, then slowly creep up.
Make a quick stop right behind the vehicle.
Stay about four car lengths behind the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay well behind the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Always stay well behind the vehicle in front of you, even when both are stopped. The vehicle could back up without warning, or you may need space to move out of the way of another vehicle coming from behind.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert you to upcoming road conditions and hazards.

questions.question: What percentage of motorcycle and car crashes happen because the driver fails to yield the right-of-way to the motorcycle?
questions.correctAnswerText: Over 50 percent
questions.explanation: More than half of motorcycle and car crashes happen because the driver fails to yield the right-of-way to the motorcycle.

questions.question: Riding on the far side of a lane when following another vehicle:

options.text: Is recommended because you will be seen easily.
Is not recommended because drivers seldom use their side mirrors and may not see you.
Is recommended because a passenger in the vehicle may tell the driver that you are there.
Is illegal because you have to ride in the center portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is not recommended because drivers seldom use their side mirrors and may not see you.
questions.explanation: Most drivers do not check their side mirrors as often as their rearview mirror. When following a car, ride in the center portion of the lane where the driver is most likely to see you in their rearview mirror.

questions.question: If you must swerve, you should:

options.text: Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
Press the handgrip in the opposite direction of the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: To swerve around a hazard, press the handlegrip in the direction you want to turn. To turn left, press the left handlegrip, then the right to recover. To turn right, press the right handlegrip, then the left.

questions.question: When an operator's left arm is bent at the elbow and pointing upward, it means the operator:
questions.correctAnswerText: Plans to turn right.
questions.explanation: Some operators use hand signals instead of turn signals to show their intent. A left arm bent at the elbow and pointing upward means the operator plans to turn right or change lanes to the right.

questions.question: The center portion of a traffic lane is where:

options.text: Debris and oil drippings from cars often collect.
Motorcycle riders should always travel for safety.
Drivers are least likely to see a motorcyclist.

questions.correctAnswerText: Debris and oil drippings from cars often collect.
questions.explanation: The centermost portion of a lane collects debris and oil drippings from cars. Other hazards like utility hole covers are also found in this area.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs that show road rules, like speed limits, are rectangular with white backgrounds and black lettering or symbols. You must follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: What can increase fatigue when riding?

options.text: Starting a ride late in the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riding in cool weather.
questions.explanation: To stay safe and avoid fatigue, dress to protect yourself from wind and rain. Ride no more than six hours per day. Take a break at least every two hours. Do not use artificial stimulants because you may feel extreme fatigue when they wear off.

questions.question: What is the correct way to swerve on a motorcycle?

options.text: Press the handle grip in the direction you plan to swerve.
Press the handle grip in the direction opposite of where you plan to swerve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handle grip in the direction you plan to swerve.
questions.explanation: To swerve and avoid a hazard, press lightly on the handle grip in the direction you want to go. To swerve left, press the left grip, then press the right grip to straighten out. To swerve right, press the right grip, then the left grip.

questions.question: What should you do if a dog chases your motorcycle?

options.text: Stop until the animal loses interest.
Approach the animal slowly, then speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Approach the animal slowly, then speed up.
questions.explanation: If a dog chases you, slow down and approach the dog calmly. Then speed up and leave it behind.

questions.question: Which part of the lane should you always avoid?

options.text: The left portion of the lane
The center portion of the lane
The right portion of the lane
No portion of the lane should always be avoided.

questions.correctAnswerText: No portion of the lane should always be avoided.
questions.explanation: There is no lane position that is always best and no lane position that you should always avoid. Choose your lane position based on current road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a benefit of riding in a tight group?

options.text: It takes up minimal space on the highway.
The group is easy to see.
The group is unlikely to be split up.
The riders will get to their destination more quickly in a close group than a group that is spread out.

questions.correctAnswerText: The riders will get to their destination more quickly in a close group than a group that is spread out.
questions.explanation: Riding in a tight group is better than riding spread out because the group takes up less road space, is easier for others to see, and is less likely to be separated at traffic lights and during passes.

questions.question: A rider wearing a helmet is _______ more likely to survive a crash than a rider without a helmet.
questions.correctAnswerText: Three times
questions.explanation: Riders who wear helmets are three times more likely to survive a crash than riders without helmets. This is true no matter what speed you are riding.

questions.question: What is the best lane position for a motorcycle?

options.text: There is no single best lane position.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is no single best lane position.
questions.explanation: There is no lane position that is always best. Change your lane position as conditions change. Choose a position that gives you more space and makes it easier for other drivers to see you.

questions.question: Studies show that nearly ______ of riders killed in motorcycle crashes had been drinking.
questions.correctAnswerText: 40 percent
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a major cause of motorcycle crashes and deaths. Nearly 40 percent of all riders killed in motorcycle crashes had been drinking.

questions.question: When braking on a slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Not use any brakes, but downshift.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, slow down and avoid sudden movements. Use both brakes if you need to slow down or stop.

questions.question: Which of the following is true?

options.text: The front and rear brakes provide equal braking power.
The front brake provides more braking power than the rear brake.
The rear brake provides more braking power than the front brake.
Only the front brake should be used when braking.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front brake provides more braking power than the rear brake.
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of the total stopping power. Always use both brakes when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: How do you brake in a straight line with maximum stopping power?

options.text: Use the front brake first, then the rear brake.
Use the rear brake first, then the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time. Do not lock either wheel.
Use both brakes at the same time. Lock the rear wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time. Do not lock either wheel.
questions.explanation: The best braking happens when you use both the front and rear brakes together without locking either wheel.

questions.question: How can you reduce your reaction time?

options.text: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
Shift into neutral when slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: When you approach a dangerous area like an intersection, position your hands on the clutch and brakes. This lets you react faster if a hazard appears.

questions.question: Who should set the speed for a group of riders?
questions.correctAnswerText: The last rider
questions.explanation: The last rider should set the pace for the group. This makes sure no one gets left behind.

questions.question: What may you need to adjust before carrying a passenger?
questions.correctAnswerText: The shocks.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds extra weight to your motorcycle. You need to adjust the shocks because the bike will sit at a different height and angle. You should also adjust the headlight and mirrors.

questions.question: What should you remember when going through a curve?

options.text: Always stay in the same lane position through the entire curve.
Always stay on the left side of the lane through the entire curve.
Always stay on the right side of the lane through the entire curve.
The best path may not follow the exact curve of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The best path may not follow the exact curve of the road.
questions.explanation: Conditions on the road can change at any time. Be ready to change your position in the lane when needed. The safest path through a curve may not match the curve of the road itself.
